review: Read the complete room media bridge, projection contracts, new lifecycle tests and unchanged hook tests. First-party browser WebRTC coordination and synthetic fixtures; no audio, credentials, personal accounts, assets or third-party implementation exported.

The existing bridge uses room participants, consent, a provider-detached mode for human voice, signaling and a separate GPT Live media boundary. Existing two-person implementation rejects the unsupported three-person voice profile before requesting a microphone.

A new six-case regression suite reproduced four failures: late microphone acquisition for participant/owner after close, late permission rejection changing the closed projection, and a late microphone after room-consent withdrawal.

The correction stops every track in a microphone stream returned to a closed bridge and returns before peer construction/signaling. Late denial leaves the closed projection intact. Normal admitted participant startup and cleanup still pass.

Existing hook tests cover waiting for teardown before replacement, closing on room identity change and explicit provider-detached human voice. These tests mock the underlying bridge; only the new lifecycle tests execute the exported bridge.
Consent, source grants, provider funding and game-action authority remain separate; this source does not grant any of them.
limits: Unfrozen private source proposal; not committed or published.
The microphone cancellation fix and its tests are newer than running R380 and require a future installed check.
Mocked media tests do not qualify attended microphone playback, Discord call, provider mixing, paid model usage or Minecraft/GPT Live context continuity.
The complete asynchronous owner-mixer restoration lifecycle remains outside this focused cancellation fix.
Existing helper modules and shared contracts remain separate preview/runtime inputs; this is not a standalone application.
